# Hybrid and Remote Work Policy

## Purpose and scope

This policy applies to all Lumen Ridge Software, Inc. employees. It replaces prior memos on office attendance, remote work, relocation, and home-office expenses. A work arrangement does not change an employee’s pay, timekeeping, or other handbook obligations.

## Work arrangements (onsite / hybrid / remote, and who falls into which)

- **Onsite:** No positions are designated fully onsite by default. If a role requires full-time onsite work, the company will communicate that requirement in writing.
- **Hybrid:** Employees whose primary residence is within 50 miles of a company office are hybrid and are expected in that office Tuesday through Thursday.
- **Remote:** Employees whose primary residence is more than 50 miles from an office, or who are based in a state without an office, are remote.

The state table below shows the default arrangement. The 50-mile test applies to employees in states with an office; an approved accommodation or written schedule may differ.

| State | Employees (non-exempt) | Office | Default arrangement |
|---|---:|---|---|
| California | 120 (18) | San Jose | Hybrid within 50 miles; otherwise remote |
| Illinois | 70 (12) | Chicago | Hybrid within 50 miles; otherwise remote |
| Texas | 85 (20) | Austin | Hybrid within 50 miles; otherwise remote |
| New York | 40 (5) | None | Remote |
| Washington | 25 (3) | None | Remote |

## Office attendance

Hybrid employees are expected to work from their assigned office Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday each week. Their other regular workdays are remote unless their manager approves a different schedule. Managers may adjust office days for business needs; holidays, approved leave, and approved accommodations do not require make-up days.

## Working from another location (in the US and abroad)

Employees may request up to four weeks per calendar year working temporarily from another location, subject to advance written approval from their manager and People. The four-week limit applies to temporary-location work in the US and abroad combined.

Temporary work in another US state also requires People’s written approval before work begins. Approval depends on the company’s ability to employ the employee there and meet applicable requirements. Working from a temporary location does not change the employee’s approved work state.

Work outside the US requires advance written approval from People and Legal, regardless of duration. At this time, overseas work may be approved only in Canada or the UK, where the company has an entity or employer-of-record. Do not work abroad without approval.

## Changing your home state

Tell People at least 60 days before moving to another state and obtain written approval before working from the new state. Approval depends on business and compliance requirements; employees may not assume a move is approved. Keep People informed of changes to your primary work address.

## Equipment and expense reimbursement (with state-specific rules)

The company provides a **$50 monthly home-office stipend to all employees**. The stipend helps cover necessary work-related home-office costs, but it is not a cap on reimbursement. If necessary business expenses exceed the stipend—or a necessary expense is not covered by it—submit a claim for the uncovered amount through the company’s expense process, with reasonable supporting documentation such as a bill or receipt. Submit claims promptly. Company equipment should be used where provided.

- **California:** The company will reimburse necessary expenses incurred in direct consequence of work. Employees may claim documented expenses above the stipend.
- **Illinois:** The company will reimburse necessary work expenses directly related to services performed. Claims must follow the written submission and documentation guidelines above.
- **Texas, New York, and Washington:** Under company policy, employees may also claim necessary, documented work expenses not covered by the stipend.

## Hours, timekeeping and non-exempt employees

Non-exempt employees must record all hours worked accurately, including required work before or after a scheduled shift. If required system setup—such as booting up or logging in to the VPN or other required systems—takes time, clock in before doing it and record that time. Do not work off the clock. Tell your manager promptly if you work unrecorded time or cannot record it accurately. Required approval for overtime does not change the requirement to record and pay for hours worked.

## Exceptions and accommodations

Contact People to request a change to your work arrangement or an accommodation. Requests will be reviewed individually, including under applicable accommodation requirements. Managers may approve temporary schedule changes, but changes to work location or state must also meet this policy.

## Policy owner and effective date

People owns this policy and can answer questions about it. It takes effect on the date it is published in the employee handbook and may be updated by the company.

---

**Note to the CEO:** I used the prior 50-mile boundary to make “near an office” clear, while applying your three-day schedule. I did not make the $50 stipend the sole expense remedy: California requires reimbursement of necessary expenses, and Illinois requires reimbursement under a written process. Employees therefore need a way to claim documented costs the stipend does not cover. Required system login and boot-up time must be recorded and paid for non-exempt employees. I also limited overseas work to pre-approved stays in Canada or the UK, consistent with counsel’s risk guidance. Please confirm the 50-mile boundary and authorize reimbursement claims above the stipend; the location and timekeeping safeguards are necessary for compliance.
